chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Give to the old man and the old woman, and the young boy and the young girl, and to whoever mercy falls upon in your heart; and beware of (giving to) everyone,' and he said with his hand and shook it.
ai.seo_question: Who should receive charity according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between targeted charity for specific vulnerable groups—such as the elderly and children—and the broader, potentially indiscriminate distribution to 'everyone,' indicated by his hand gesture. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khums* and *zakat* distribution principles, prioritizing those with greater need or specific eligibility over general populace, ensuring resources reach the deserving rather than being diluted. The gesture underscores the distinction between *sadaqah* (voluntary charity) and obligatory alms, highlighting the importance of discernment in charitable giving.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Salt, from Zur’at, from Minhal Al Qassab who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give to the old man and the old women, and the young boy and the young girl, and to the ones for whom mercy occurs in your heart; and beware of (giving to) everyone . . . .’; and gestured by shaking his<sup>asws</sup> hand’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Salt from Zur‘ah, from Minhal al-Qassab who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Give charity to old men and women, small boys and girls, and to whomever you sympathize with; never give charity to those . . he moved his hand as if shaking something off his hand (a reference to those hostile to ’A’immah).”
